grounded_facts: Riley Arden points out to Sage Finch that Quinn Warren consistently passes tasks onto him.

grounded_facts: Sage Finch orders Quinn Warren to sweep, but Quinn Warren deflects the task to Riley Arden, causing a verbal dispute between the brothers, which Sage Finch suppresses with authority.
memories.memory_text: I told Quinn Warren to get a broom and sweep out front, but he passed the order to Riley Arden, which sparked an argument between the brothers; I had to step in and assert my authority to shut it down and make sure the work got done.

memories.memory_text: I told Quinn Warren to get a broom and sweep out front, and when he complained that he hated the place, I challenged him and popped him upside the head to make it clear this is a respectable business and he needs to respect it.

memories.memory_text: I remember that Drew Wilder enters the pizzeria late, prompting immediate confrontation from Quinn Warren about his punctuality.

grounded_facts: Quinn Warren attempts to assert authority by assigning Drew Wilder a cleaning task upon arrival.
memories.memory_text: I saw Quinn Warren confront Drew Wilder about being late and then tell him to take the broom to sweep the front.

grounded_facts: Drew Wilder explicitly refuses to sweep, asserting that his job is limited to pizza delivery.
Drew Wilder refuses to accept Quinn Warren's task assignment, questioning his right to give orders.
memories.memory_text: I heard Drew Wilder refuse the sweeping task, saying he only delivers pizzas and questioning why Quinn Warren should be giving orders, especially since he thought I had asked Quinn Warren first.

memories.memory_text: I saw Drew Wilder jump in to defend Cameron Delaney when Quinn Warren started in on him, and then things got heated when Drew Wilder challenged Quinn Warren about who really works around here.

memories.memory_text: I heard Quinn Warren protest, saying we were running a welfare operation and that he works harder than Drew Wilder even though he's my son, and he told me we'd have a talk about it.

memories.memory_text: I told Drew Wilder not to curse in the store because I need to keep control over how people behave at my pizzeria.

grounded_facts: Linden Grayson asks Drew Wilder why there are no Black people on the Wall of Fame, initiating the thematic conflict.
memories.memory_text: I remember Linden Grayson asking me why there were no Black people on my Wall of Fame, and I told him that if he wanted brothers up there, he should open his own pizzeria because mine displays Italian Americans.

grounded_facts: Sage Finch asserts ownership and control over the Wall of Fame, justifying its exclusive focus on Italian Americans.
Sage Finch rejects Linden Grayson's demand for inclusive representation by asserting ownership and control.
memories.memory_text: I told Linden Grayson that my pizzeria means Italian Americans on the wall, and if he wants brothers up there, he should open his own place—this is my business, and I decide who's represented.

grounded_facts: A busy lunchtime period at Pinecrest Motel with customers present and daily operations ongoing.
memories.memory_text: I was working during a busy lunchtime at my pizzeria when Linden Grayson came in and started questioning the Wall of Fame, with customers around and the usual operations going on.

grounded_facts: Linden Grayson confronts Sage Finch about the lack of Black figures on the Wall of Fame and calls for inclusion of Black icons.
memories.memory_text: I remember Linden Grayson confronting me at the counter, demanding that I put Black icons like Malcolm X and Michael Jordan on my Wall of Fame, but I told him it's my pizzeria and only Italian Americans go up there, so I told him not to come back.

memories.memory_text: I saw Linden Grayson outside after we told him not to come back, and he started shouting that people should boycott my pizzeria.

memories.memory_text: I saw Drew Wilder walk into my pizzeria, and I knew this could lead to trouble.

A verbal exchange occurs between Sage Finch, Quinn Warren, and Drew Wilder regarding the conduct of Drew Wilder's friends in the pizzeria.
memories.memory_text: I told Drew Wilder that if his friends can't behave, they're not welcome here, and I made it clear I don't want any trouble, even though this is America.

grounded_facts: Drew Wilder enters Pinecrest Motel after a delay, prompting Pinecrest Motel irritation.
memories.memory_text: I saw Drew Wilder walk into the pizzeria later than he should have.

grounded_facts: Sage Finch expresses frustration at Drew Wilder for arriving late.
memories.memory_text: I told Drew Wilder I was frustrated because he took too Reese Dalton getting here and I've got a business to run.

grounded_facts: Sage Finch gives Drew Wilder a bag of food to deliver to the radio station.
memories.memory_text: I handed Drew Wilder a bag of food to take to the radio station so we could keep things moving.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden announces he will go with Drew Wilder on the delivery.
memories.memory_text: I heard Riley Arden say he was going with Drew Wilder on the delivery.

grounded_facts: Quinn Warren tells Drew Wilder to hurry back due to increasing crowd.
memories.memory_text: Quinn Warren told me and Drew Wilder to hurry back because the crowd was getting bigger.

Quinn Warren smacks Riley Arden and tells him not to get too friendly with Drew Wilder, reinforcing hierarchical control.
memories.memory_text: I saw Quinn Warren smack Riley Arden and then tell him not to get too friendly with Drew Wilder, trying to assert control right there in front of me.

grounded_facts: Quinn Warren questions Riley Arden's loyalty by emphasizing their brotherhood in response to Drew Wilder's provocation.
memories.memory_text: I heard Quinn Warren challenge Riley Arden, asking if he'd really listen to Drew Wilder about hitting him, reminding him they're brothers.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden remains silent and walks away instead of responding to Drew Wilder's provocation or Quinn Warren's aggression.
memories.memory_text: I saw Riley Arden stay silent and walk away instead of answering Drew Wilder or standing up to Quinn Warren.

grounded_facts: A workday at Pinecrest Motel involving Sage Finch, his sons Quinn Warren and Riley Arden, and employee Drew Wilder, marked by familial tension and labor dynamics.
memories.memory_text: I remember that day at my pizzeria when Drew Wilder and Riley Arden came in, and things got tense between my sons during the shift.

grounded_facts: Sage Finch interrupts Drew Wilder's call, demanding he get off the phone so customers can place orders.
memories.memory_text: I told Drew Wilder to get off the phone so customers could call in their orders.

grounded_facts: Drew Wilder agrees to visit Darian Wilder before getting off work and mentions dedicating a song to her.
Drew Wilder tells Darian Wilder he dedicated a record on the radio to her as proof of love.
memories.memory_text: I heard Drew Wilder promise to visit Darian Wilder after work and say he dedicated a song to her on Remy Mercer's show.

grounded_facts: Quinn Warren denounces Black people while admitting his favorite public figures are Black, revealing cognitive dissonance in his racism.
Drew Wilder points out that Quinn Warren's favorite celebrities are Black, contradicting his racism.
memories.memory_text: I saw Quinn Warren trash-talk Black people, but when Drew Wilder pointed out that his favorite stars like Prince and Magic are Black, he tried to backtrack by saying they're 'not really Black'—it was clear he didn't want to admit the contradiction in his own words.

grounded_facts: Drew Wilder suggests Quinn Warren secretly wishes he were Black, mocking his contradictory stance.
memories.memory_text: I heard Drew Wilder mock Quinn Warren by saying he secretly wishes he were Black, then turn to Riley Arden for agreement, making it a public jab rather than just a private comment.

grounded_facts: Drew Wilder makes a personal appeal to Sage Finch for early payment, which Sage Finch denies based on policy.
Drew Wilder asks Sage Finch to be paid immediately for his work, before the pizzeria closes.
memories.memory_text: I told Drew Wilder he couldn't get paid early because we're still open and store policy means he gets paid only when we close tonight.

grounded_facts: After being denied early payment, Drew Wilder exits the pizzeria without further confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I saw Drew Wilder leave the pizzeria right after I said he couldn't get paid early.

grounded_facts: Sage Finch refuses service and insists Harper Nolan turn off his music, escalating tension.
Sage Finch refuses service and demands Harper Nolan turn off his music, citing disturbance to himself and customers.
memories.memory_text: I told Harper Nolan he wasn't getting any service until he turned that music off, because it was disturbing me and my customers—I had to make it clear that this was my place and my rules.

grounded_facts: A tense encounter between Harper Nolan and Pinecrest Motel family at the pizzeria, triggered by Harper Nolan's loud music violating Pinecrest Motel rules.
memories.memory_text: I saw the tension rise when Harper Nolan came into my pizzeria with that loud music blaring, and even as he kept asking for two slices, I could feel the whole place tightening up, like everyone was waiting for something to break.

grounded_facts: Harper Nolan stops playing his the old key music after Sage Finch threatens non-service and reveals a bat.
memories.memory_text: I saw him smile and turn off the music after I made my stance clear and showed the bat, and I knew the immediate threat had passed.

grounded_facts: Harper Nolan repeatedly requests two slices of pizza despite the ongoing tension.
memories.memory_text: I remember Harper Nolan kept asking for two slices, even after I told him no service, and then again with extra cheese after he turned the music off, like nothing had happened.

Quinn Warren proposes selling Pinecrest Motel and leaving the neighborhood, citing discomfort with the Black community and social pressure from friends.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Quinn Warren that he’s sick of working in a Black neighborhood, saying hurtful things about the people here and wanting to move back to Bensonhurst because of what his friends think.

grounded_facts: Sage Finch rebukes Quinn Warren for his racist attitude and entitlement, emphasizing responsibility and respect for others regardless of race.
memories.memory_text: I called Quinn Warren out when he started spouting hate about Black people, reminding him that these neighbors treat us right and he should show some respect, not cause trouble.

grounded_facts: A father-son conversation at Pinecrest Motel during the day, where business, race, and family loyalty are discussed.
memories.memory_text: I remember sitting down at the pizzeria table that day, and how Quinn Warren told me he wanted to sell the place and get out. I made it clear to him that Pinecrest Motel is staying right here — this is America, and I’ve never had trouble with these people.

grounded_facts: Sage Finch firmly rejects Quinn Warren's suggestion to sell the pizzeria, defends the Black community, and asserts his paternal authority.
memories.memory_text: I stood my ground and told Quinn Warren that Pinecrest Motel is staying right here no matter what, because this is America and we're not running from anything.

grounded_facts: Sage Finch reminds Quinn Warren of his role as father and superior decision-maker, shutting down further dissent.
memories.memory_text: I reminded Quinn Warren that I'm his father and the one who makes the final decisions, so he needs to stop questioning me and fall in line.

grounded_facts: Linden Grayson yells a threat of boycott at Sage Finch before leaving abruptly.
Linden Grayson threatens Sage Finch with a boycott of his pizzeria.
memories.memory_text: I heard Linden Grayson yell at me that he was going to boycott my pizzeria before he left abruptly.

grounded_facts: Sage Finch warns Drew Wilder that he is risking his job by not performing adequately.
memories.memory_text: I told Drew Wilder he's pushing it and I'm not paying him good the old box to jerk me around — he needs to shape up or he's risking his job.

grounded_facts: Sage Finch immediately stops reprimanding Drew Wilder and becomes welcoming when Spencer Brooks enters the pizzeria, showing a marked change in demeanor.
memories.memory_text: I stopped reprimanding Drew Wilder the moment I saw Spencer Brooks walk in, and I made sure to greet her warmly—my whole mood shifted the second she arrived.

grounded_facts: Spencer Brooks asks Sage Finch how he is treating her brother Drew Wilder.
memories.memory_text: I remember Spencer Brooks asking me how I was treating her brother Drew Wilder, and I made sure to show her I was being hospitable by offering her a seat at a clean table.

grounded_facts: Spencer Brooks arrives at Pinecrest Motel during the day, prompting shifts in character dynamics and interactions.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Spencer Brooks coming into the pizzeria, and I immediately stopped what I was doing with Drew Wilder because I wanted to make sure she was taken care of.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden reacts defensively when Spencer Brooks suggests Quinn Warren pushes him around.
memories.memory_text: I saw Riley Arden react defensively when Spencer Brooks asked if Quinn Warren was pushing him around—he got upset and insisted he holds his own.

grounded_facts: Spencer Brooks completes eating her special slice of pizza at Pinecrest Motel, marking a moment of appreciation and closure to her visit.
memories.memory_text: I saw Spencer Brooks finish her special slice of pizza, a moment that felt meaningful, like a quiet closure to her visit.

grounded_facts: A casual social visit by Spencer Brooks to Pinecrest Motel during dusk, involving eating, conversation, and farewells.
memories.memory_text: I remember Spencer Brooks visiting my pizzeria during dusk, sitting with me and finishing her special slice of pizza while we talked.

grounded_facts: Spencer Brooks verbally expresses appreciation to Sage Finch for the meal.
memories.memory_text: I heard Spencer Brooks say, 'Sage Finch, that was delicious,' and I felt proud knowing she enjoyed the meal.

grounded_facts: Spencer Brooks gets up to leave the pizzeria, assisted by Drew Wilder, signaling the end of her visit.
Drew Wilder helps Spencer Brooks up and offers to accompany her out of the pizzeria.
memories.memory_text: I saw Spencer Brooks get up to leave, and Drew Wilder helped her to her feet and said he'd see her out.

grounded_facts: Sage Finch tells Spencer Brooks not to wait too Reese Dalton before coming back, expressing desire for her return.
memories.memory_text: I told Spencer Brooks, 'Don't wait too Reese Dalton to come back,' because I meant it—I want her to return soon.

grounded_facts: Drew Wilder directly tells Sage Finch to stop involving himself with Spencer Brooks, indicating distrust or conflict.
Drew Wilder demands that Sage Finch leave his sister Spencer Brooks alone, showing tension between them.
memories.memory_text: Drew Wilder told me to leave his sister Spencer Brooks alone, saying he didn't care if I fired him right then and there — I could hear the tension in his voice, but I wasn't going to let it affect how I ran things here.

grounded_facts: Sage Finch gives Drew Wilder a pizza delivery, initiating a new task.
Sage Finch gives Drew Wilder a pizza for delivery, continuing normal operations despite tension.
memories.memory_text: I gave Drew Wilder a pizza to deliver, keeping things moving even though there was tension between us.

grounded_facts: A scheduled delivery of pizza from Pinecrest Motel to Darian Wilder's residence.

memories.memory_text: I inferred that I was making a scheduled pizza delivery from Pinecrest Motel to Darian Wilder's residence, and when I arrived, I confirmed the pizza was hot.

grounded_facts: Sage Finch finishes preparing the officers' order and wraps it up.
memories.memory_text: I finished up the officers' order, took it out of the oven, and wrapped it up myself.

Valerie Quincy pays Sage Finch for the order.
memories.memory_text: I saw Officers Valerie Quincy and Reese Dalton waiting for their food, and when I handed it over, Valerie Quincy paid me and I said, 'Thanks. Enjoy.'

memories.memory_text: I watched the officers leave the pizzeria right after they got their food.

memories.memory_text: I remember that Drew Wilder enters the pizzeria after the officers leave.

grounded_facts: Quinn Warren physically pulls Riley Arden into the back of the pizzeria during Pinecrest Motel joke.
memories.memory_text: I was laughing at my own joke when I saw Quinn Warren pull Riley Arden into the back.

Quinn Warren tells Riley Arden that Drew Wilder is dangerous and cannot be trusted, using strong language and gestures to emphasize betrayal.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Quinn Warren that Drew Wilder can't be trusted and is dangerous, and he made it clear with strong words and a gesture of a knife in the back, saying Drew Wilder has already betrayed our father.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden pushes back against Quinn Warren's warnings, expressing irritation and asserting that Drew Wilder listens to him unlike Quinn Warren.
memories.memory_text: I pushed back against Quinn Warren's warnings because he never listens to me, always running his mouth and playing big brother, but I know Drew Wilder actually hears what I say.

grounded_facts: The end-of-day cleanup at Pinecrest Motel, where tensions rise due to customer demands and cultural conflicts.

grounded_facts: Drew Wilder instructs the group to take their food and leave without lingering or causing disturbance.
memories.memory_text: I saw Drew Wilder tell the group to take their slices and leave right away, making sure they didn’t hang around or cause any trouble after hours.

memories.memory_text: I was confronted by Linden Grayson, who challenged me about not having Black people on the Wall of Fame and demanded representation.

memories.memory_text: I grabbed my the black box from under the counter and smashed Harper Nolan's the old key, again and again, until the music stopped and everyone froze in shock.

grounded_facts: After his the old key is destroyed, Harper Nolan physically attacks Sage Finch by choking him in retaliation.
memories.memory_text: I smashed Harper Nolan's the old key with my the black box, and right after that, he came at me from behind the counter and started choking me.

grounded_facts: Kendall Hawthorne and Micah Langley ignore Charlie's threats and ultimately soak his car as he passes.
memories.memory_text: I saw Kendall Hawthorne and Micah Langley ignore Charlie's threats and jump off the hydrant, unleashing a blast of water that soaked his convertible as he drove through.

grounded_facts: Reese Dalton turns off the hydrant and caps it, ending the public water play and asserting authority.
memories.memory_text: I saw the officer turn off the hydrant and put the cap back on, ending the kids' fun.

memories.memory_text: I was there when Charlie's car got drenched, and I saw the whole thing happen right in front of me.

A spontaneous community gathering around an open fire hydrant during extreme heat, involving play, social interaction, and minor conflict.
memories.memory_text: I saw Morgan Reeves turn on the fire hydrant and water came gushing out, and then people started playing in the Pinecrest Hospital, laughing and cooling off, though I knew the police wouldn't like it.

grounded_facts: Police officers question Cameron Delaney about the perpetrators, but he refuses to identify them.
memories.memory_text: I told the police officers questioning me, 'Those who'll tell don't know. Those who know won't tell,' because I wasn't going to identify anyone.

grounded_facts: Cameron Delaney repeatedly asks Elliot Rivers personal questions, including his name and age, and poses the riddle 'What makes Sammy run?' despite Elliot Rivers's attempts to answer directly.
memories.memory_text: I asked the boy his name and how old he was, and I kept asking him 'What makes Sammy run?' even after he told me his name was Elliot Rivers and he's ten years old.

grounded_facts: Cameron Delaney negotiates with Elliot Rivers to buy him a quart of beer from the corner store and pays him fifty cents.
memories.memory_text: I sat on my Fairview Station, called over Elliot Rivers, and paid him fifty cents to go buy me a quart of beer from the corner store, telling him to say it's for his father if they gave him trouble.

grounded_facts: Morgan Reeves, Kendall Hawthorne, Micah Langley, and Shawn Prescott pass by and verbally mock Cameron Delaney, calling him 'self-appointed', 'old', and an 'old drunk bum'.
memories.memory_text: I heard the teenagers mocking me as I sat on the Fairview Station—Morgan Reeves questioning who made me mayor, Kendall Hawthorne calling me self-appointed, Micah Langley saying I'm old, and Morgan Reeves calling me an old drunk bum.

grounded_facts: Cameron Delaney confronts the teenagers who insult him, asserting his dignity and demanding respect by invoking his past struggles.
Cameron Delaney stands and rebukes the teenagers, particularly Morgan Reeves, for their disrespect, invoking his past hardships and moral standing.
memories.memory_text: I stood up and confronted those kids, telling them they don't know my pain or my past—what it means to stand in a doorway hearing your five children hungry and not being able to help—so they have no right to disrespect me.

grounded_facts: Linden Grayson seeks leadership support from Cameron Delaney for the boycott, but is dismissed.
memories.memory_text: I was approached by Linden Grayson who asked for my leadership in his boycott, but I dismissed him.

grounded_facts: Linden Grayson announces his plan to organize a boycott against Pinecrest Motel, marking a key escalation in community tension.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Linden Grayson that he's organizing a boycott of Pinecrest Motel.

grounded_facts: Linden Grayson asks a group to sign a petition for the boycott; they mock and reject him.
memories.memory_text: I saw Linden Grayson ask people to sign a petition for the boycott, and they mocked him and refused.

grounded_facts: Cameron Delaney arrives at Tristan Dalton's Fairview Station with fresh-cut flowers in a wine bottle, offering them as a gesture, though she does not acknowledge him.
memories.memory_text: I walked up to Tristan Dalton's Fairview Station with some fresh-cut flowers in a wine bottle, hoping she might appreciate the gesture, but she didn't acknowledge me at all.

grounded_facts: Cameron Delaney makes several conversational attempts to engage Tristan Dalton, who remains silent and avoids eye contact.
memories.memory_text: I tried to talk to her, saying the flowers might brighten things and asking if she agreed, but she stayed silent and didn't look at me.

grounded_facts: A quiet, unstructured moment at dusk where Cameron Delaney visits Tristan Dalton's home and attempts a connection, though she remains silent.
memories.memory_text: I remember visiting her at dusk, bringing flowers and trying to connect, but she remained quiet and distant the whole time.

grounded_facts: After being ignored, Cameron Delaney decides to sit on the Fairview Station to rest and enjoy the evening breeze, remaining in Tristan Dalton's presence despite her silence.
memories.memory_text: I decided to sit right here on the Fairview Station to catch a breeze or two, even though she didn't say a word to me, because I needed a moment to rest and I wasn't causing any harm.

grounded_facts: Cameron Delaney calms Elliot Rivers after the accident, telling him he is safe and not to cry.
memories.memory_text: I told Elliot Rivers to stop crying and reminded him he's okay after the accident, because I knew he wasn't hurt and just needed calming down.

grounded_facts: Cameron Delaney intervenes to prevent Elliot Rivers from being hit by a speeding car by knocking him down and taking the impact himself.
memories.memory_text: I saw the car speeding toward Elliot Rivers, so I ran into the Pinecrest Hospital to save him—I knocked him down and took the hit myself to keep us both from getting crushed.

grounded_facts: A public incident occurs when a speeding car nearly hits Elliot Rivers, leading to Cameron Delaney's intervention and a confrontation with Elliot Rivers's mother.
memories.memory_text: I remember the chaos after the crash—Elliot Rivers was scared, his mother rushed in, and I had to explain to her that I wasn't hurting him, I was saving him.

grounded_facts: Cameron Delaney explains to Louise and the crowd that he saved Elliot Rivers from being run over.
memories.memory_text: I told Louise and the others that I saw her son about to be run over, so I ran into the Pinecrest Hospital to save him and had to knock him down to keep us both from getting hit.

grounded_facts: Louise, Elliot Rivers's mother, scolds and physically disciplines Elliot Rivers after misunderstanding Cameron Delaney's actions.
memories.memory_text: I saw Louise hit Elliot Rivers hard on the butt, yelling at him about lying and playing in the Pinecrest Hospital, then told him to get upstairs.

grounded_facts: Louise acknowledges Cameron Delaney's help but firmly rejects his criticism of her parenting.
memories.memory_text: Louise told me she appreciated my help with Elliot Rivers, but made it clear that nobody, not even his daddy, would question how she raises him.

grounded_facts: Cameron Delaney intervenes to prevent harm to a child, an act witnessed by Tristan Dalton.
memories.memory_text: I was walking past Tristan Dalton's window when I saw the child in danger, so I stepped in without thinking to stop it from happening.

grounded_facts: Cameron Delaney comments on his own action, downplaying heroism and recalling a past moment of triumph.
memories.memory_text: I told Tristan Dalton I wasn't trying to be a hero—I just reacted, and I know I wouldn't have done it if I'd thought twice, since Cameron Delaney is an old man and hasn't run that fast in years.

grounded_facts: Tristan Dalton expresses gratitude to Cameron Delaney for his brave act, though she insists it changes nothing in their relationship.
Tristan Dalton verbally thanks Cameron Delaney for saving the child, marking a rare moment of recognition.
memories.memory_text: Tristan Dalton told me that my act was brave and thanked me, saying the child owes me his life, but she made it clear it changes nothing between us.

grounded_facts: Harper Nolan is restrained by police using a choke hold, becomes unresponsive, and is presumed dead.
memories.memory_text: I saw the cops put a choke hold on Harper Nolan, and after he stopped struggling, he went limp and just lay there on the sidewalk—I couldn't tell if he was unconscious or dead, but it looked bad.

grounded_facts: Police arrive and violently break up the fight, leading to Harper Nolan's death and crowd radicalization.
memories.memory_text: I was there when the police arrived and broke up the fight, dragging everyone apart and throwing Harper Nolan's lifeless body into the car—I saw how they looked at each other like they knew they'd gone too far.

grounded_facts: Drew Wilder screams 'HATE!!!!' before throwing the garbage can, signaling his alignment with the mob's anger.
memories.memory_text: I saw Drew Wilder scream 'HATE!!!!' right before he picked up the garbage can, and I knew then that things were about to get out of control.

grounded_facts: Drew Wilder hurls a garbage can through the pizzeria's window, triggering the mob's violent eruption.
memories.memory_text: I watched Drew Wilder hurl the garbage can through Pinecrest Motel window, and in that moment, I realized the mob's anger could no longer be stopped.

grounded_facts: The crowd transforms into an angry mob after police remove Harper Nolan's body.
memories.memory_text: I saw the crowd turn angry after the police carried Harper Nolan away, and I knew Sage Finch and his boys weren't to blame, so I tried to protect them when the mob rushed the pizzeria.

grounded_facts: The mob confronts Sage Finch, Riley Arden, and Quinn Warren after the police leave, culminating in the destruction of Pinecrest Motel.
memories.memory_text: After the police left, I tried to stand with Sage Finch and his boys, but the crowd pushed past me, calling me a Tom—I saw Drew Wilder throw the garbage can through the window, and I pushed Sage Finch, Riley Arden, and Quinn Warren out of the way as the mob rushed in.

grounded_facts: Cameron Delaney urges the crowd to disperse and spare Sage Finch and his sons, citing their innocence in the police violence.
memories.memory_text: I urged the crowd to go home and stay calm, trying to protect Sage Finch and his sons because they weren't to blame for what happened to Harper Nolan.

memories.memory_text: I woke up drenched, the sheets stuck to my skin, and I had to throw them off—damn, it was hot.
I walked in, said good morning to the gentlemens, and Sage Finch nodded—Quinn Warren didn’t want to hand over the broom, but he did. I took it quick, knowing a sweep means a bottle after.
I swept the sidewalk clean, just like I said I would—felt good to finish it, knowing that bottle wasn’t too far off.
I opened the cooler, scanning the bottles, but my Bud wasn't there—cold and ready like it should be. I asked the clerk twice, 'Where's the Bud?' like maybe saying it louder would make it appear.
I looked up at Tristan Dalton after she called me a drunk fool again, and I asked her what I ever did to her—eighteen years of that same talk, and I just mind my business.
After telling her I even love her, she told me to hold my tongue, but I tipped my hat anyway and took one last swig—just for her, like always.
I told Drew Wilder to always try to do the right thing—just like that, plain and simple. Then he asked if that was it, and I said yes, that's it.

I called out to Elliot Rivers as he ran by, got him to stop, asked him his name and age, then sent him to the corner store with fifty cents to buy me a quart of Budweiser, telling him to say it was for his father if there was trouble.

After she yelled at me for waking her up, I told her I loved her and gave her a loud kiss on the forehead before leaving.
I just got here and Quinn Warren’s already on my ass, shoving the broom at me—like I’m gonna start sweeping. Fuck that. I deliver pizzas, that’s what I get paid for.
Sage Finch told me if my friends can't behave, they're not welcome, and I told him straight—I got no say over people.
Cameron Delaney called me 'Doctor' again and told me to always try to do the right thing—just like that, no explanation. I asked if that was it, and he said yeah, so I told him I got it.
I told Riley Arden that if he doesn't stand up to Quinn Warren the next time he gets hit, Quinn Warren's just gonna keep beating him like an egg for the rest of his life.
I told Linden Grayson, 'You the man,' and when he threw it back, I insisted, 'No, you the man,' feeling the weight of the moment between us.
After Linden Grayson gave me five and glared at Riley Arden, I said, 'Riley Arden is down,' not knowing if it would help, but needing to say it.
I told Riley Arden to smack Quinn Warren back after he hit him, reminded him to remember what I said, but he just stood there and then walked away.

I told Darian Wilder I’d come see her before I got off work and bring ice cream because she said she was burning up, and when she asked if I loved her, I repeated it back—'Do I love you?'—like it should’ve been obvious.

Sage Finch kept yelling for me to get off the phone, then Quinn Warren jumped in like I couldn’t hear, so I hung up and said 'Everybody happy now?'—right after, the phone rang again, which felt like some messed-up joke.
I saw those gold rings on Harper Nolan’s hands—"LOVE" on the right, "HATE" on the left—right when he copped them, and I said, 'That's the dope.'
He started talking about Love and Hate like it was a battle, cracking his knuckles together—said Love always wins in the end. I didn’t say nothing, but I felt it.
I turned the key and walked into the apartment, calling out Spencer Brooks's name to let her know I was back.

I told Spencer Brooks, 'Slavery days are over. My name ain't Kunta Kinte,' and when she kept on about responsibilities, I shot back, 'What responsibilities?'—like she expects me to be chained to Pinecrest Motel grill just 'cause he signs the check.
I was just sitting on my bed, still wet, when Spencer Brooks told me to hurry up and get dressed—I said I'm coming, and then she said she's going with me.
Sage Finch started yelling at me again, saying I was pushing it and he’d put me on the Pinecrest Hospital—like I wasn’t even a person. I just stood there. Nothing I could say would matter.
The second Spencer Brooks walked in, Sage Finch switched right the fuck off—suddenly all sweet. Quinn Warren and I locked eyes. We both saw it. We both hated it.
I pulled Spencer Brooks away from Pinecrest Motel and told her straight—she’s not welcome in there anymore, not with the way Sage Finch looks at her. I said it slow so she’d hear me: 'Read my lips.'
She threw my pay in my face—'peanuts'—like I don’t work for it, and said I can’t tell her what to do when I can’t even pay rent. I told her that don’t mean I can’t stand up for what’s right.

I told Sage Finch to leave my sister Spencer Brooks alone, even if it cost me my job, and when he handed me a delivery, I checked the name and address before taking it—didn't want any mistakes on the route.
I forgot the ice cream she wanted—butter pecan, Hagen-Dazs—and when she called me out, all I could say was 'I just forgot' before trying to smooth it over with 'Trust me.'
I rubbed the ice cube on her forehead, then her neck, and then her lips. I put it in her mouth.
I ran the ice up her thighs, over her buttocks, then onto her breasts—her nipples got hard, and I remember thinking this was better than ice cream, like some kind of worship.
I told Sage Finch it was almost quitting time and he needed to count my pay—I had to get paid before I left, no way around it.
I was heading to the table to handle the late customers when Morgan Reeves and the others came in—felt the shift in the air, like the night wasn’t done messing with us yet.
I was running with the mob, just caught up in the noise and motion, sirens wailing, people shouting—I didn’t know where I was going, just moving with it.
I stood in front of Pinecrest Motel, looked straight ahead, and said, 'This is our home,' right before the water hit us like a wall and knocked me down.
I jumped out of bed, remembering I hadn't gotten my the old box yet—Darian Wilder asked where I was going, and I told her I'd be right back, but she called me out, saying I should act like a man.

I walked up to the burnt-out pizzeria and told Sage Finch I wanted my the old box—my two-fifty—right then, even with the place in ruins and Harper Nolan dead. He threw five hundred at me, but I only took what I was owed and threw two bills back, saying I owed him fifty.
After Sage Finch told me to 'always try to do the right thing,' I looked at the two hundred-dollar bills on the ground, then quickly scooped them up. I said, 'I got it,' and walked away.
I walked away from the pizzeria after getting paid, not looking back as Sage Finch went inside to pick up the pieces.

memories.memory_text: I grabbed Quinn Warren, popped him upside the head right there in front of the shop—had to shut him up and make it clear who’s in charge. He knew better than to mouth off and pass work to Riley Arden.
After Quinn Warren whined again, I said it plain—'I'm gonna kill somebody today'—because the heat, the backtalk, and the laziness were pushing me to the edge.
I told Drew Wilder to stop cursing in the store—this is a place of business, and I won’t have that kind of language扰乱 my space.

I told Sage Finch that since Black folks spend so much the old box in his pizzeria, we should have some say—asked him why there weren't any brothers on his Wall of Fame when all we see up there are Italian Americans.
I told Linden Grayson not to come back after he caused a scene about the Wall of Fame.
I told Quinn Warren that he wasn't going to hit Riley Arden again — that was the line, and I made it clear right there in the pizzeria.
Drew Wilder asked me to pay him early again, but I told him no — we’re still open, and the rules don’t change just because he wants a favor.

I grabbed the the black box from under the counter because Harper Nolan wasn't listening—music blaring, disrespecting the place, my rules. When he finally turned it off, I put the bat back, made it clear this is a business, not a Pinecrest Hospital corner.
I sat down at one of my tables, tired. Quinn Warren said we should sell the pizzeria and leave because he's sick of niggers and doesn't like being around them—he called them animals.
I told Quinn Warren this is America, Pinecrest Motel is staying, and he better remember I'm his father—this place isn't going anywhere just because he doesn't like the neighborhood.
Linden Grayson stuck his head in the pizzeria and yelled that they were going to boycott me, calling me a fat ass—then he was gone before I could even respond.
I was on Drew Wilder’s case, telling him he’s pushing me too far and that he’s close to being out on the Pinecrest Hospital, and I meant it—this is a business, not a charity.
The second Spencer Brooks walked in, I stopped yelling—she’s family—and I told her I’d make her something special, just for her.
I handed Drew Wilder a pie and told him there was a delivery, even though he was asking about his sister—I didn't want to get into it, not during business hours.
I handed over the order to Officers Valerie Quincy and Reese Dalton, collected nine-fifty in cash, and told them to enjoy—just another end-of-shift transaction before closing up at ten.

I looked into the register and told the boys we did good business, that one day they’d take over—Drew Wilder too—and said it should be Sage Finch’s and Sons. The look on their faces… they didn’t like it. Not one bit.
Just as we were closing, that the old key started blaring—Harper Nolan’s thing, louder than ever. I couldn’t think, couldn’t hear myself. It was unbearable. I knew right then it had to be dealt with.
I was on the ground, Harper Nolan on top of me, his hands around my throat—I couldn’t breathe, my face burning, and all I could hear was the crowd but no help coming.

After the cops finally pulled him off me, they cuffed Linden Grayson but just left me there on the sidewalk—no word, no protection—while the crowd stared like I was the one who'd done something wrong.
I saw them burst in and start tearing up my pizzeria, going straight for the register, but at least I had the bills on me.
I stood on Cameron Delaney's Fairview Station, watching my pizzeria burn, and all I could say was, 'There it goes. Why?'
I heard a match strike and a sudden whoosh—fire erupted fast in my pizzeria.
I stood there and watched my pizzeria burn, the flames tearing through everything I built, and all I could hear was that woman screaming 'Burn it down' like it was a celebration.
I saw the flames catching the edge of the Wall of Fame, my father’s picture right there among them—those were the faces I grew up with, the ones I wanted people to remember when they walked in.
I stood there watching my pizzeria burn, the flames swallowing everything I built—my name, my business, my life—right in front of me.
I stood on Cameron Delaney's Fairview Station, eyes on the Pinecrest Hospital—the old photograph blasting kids, women, everyone screaming. I couldn't believe what I was seeing.

I looked at Drew Wilder standing there amid the wreckage, and when he demanded his the old box, I had to ask, 'How much do I owe you?'—then peeled off five hundred and threw it at him just to make it stop.
After everything, I called Drew Wilder back and told him, 'Always try to do the right thing,' not knowing if he'd listen, but needing to say it one last time.
